extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors submitting preprints to arXiv (arXiv account holders)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and procedural rules describing the possible statuses a new submission or update can have on arXiv (incomplete, processing, submitted, on hold, expiration), what they mean, and what actions are permitted or required at each status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incomplete
rubrics_metrics.description: Not submitted — the article is in process but not yet submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may still edit the submission while it is incomplete; editing will update the expiration date. Submissions left incomplete past the expiration date will be deleted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Already submitted and being analyzed by arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During processing arXiv analyzes the submission before setting the status to either 'submitted' or (if issues are detected) 'on hold'. You may not edit the submission while it is in processing. Generally, processing is for a relatively short time period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitted (awaiting announcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the queue to be announced — the submission is set to be posted based on the automated announcement schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the final status before announcement for new submissions and replacements once you have verified format and finalized all metadata. Note that all submissions go through automated and human checks as part of moderation, which may cause delays. You may select the Unsubmit icon to remove it from this status and return it to 'incomplete'.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Hold
rubrics_metrics.description: Undergoing checks — the submission has been flagged by automated or human quality assurance and is 'on hold'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv editors will either email you with instructions on how to resolve the hold or resolve the hold without your needing to do anything. If your submission is on hold, no action is required at that time. The process may take several days. On hold submissions will not expire. Do not make a duplicate submission while your work is on hold; deleting and resubmitting will lead to further delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expiration (incomplete removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic deletion of incomplete submissions after a time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you neither submit nor update your submission within 14 days it will be removed. Any update to your submission prevents automatic removal and resets the 14-day expiration period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderation / Quality Assurance Checks
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions undergo a series of automated and human quality assurance checks as part of moderation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These checks may result in a delay or place the submission 'on hold'. Editors may contact you via the email address in your user account if follow up is required, or they may resolve issues without contacting you.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalize format and metadata before submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Before moving to the announced queue, verify that the intended submission appears in the format you desire and that all metadata are finalized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For new submissions and replacements: once you have verified format and finalized metadata, the 'submitted' status is the final status before announcement. Use the Unsubmit option if you need to revert to edit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing permissions and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: What you can or cannot do to a submission in each status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may edit while in 'incomplete' status. You may not edit during 'processing'. You may Unsubmit a 'submitted' item to return it to 'incomplete' for editing. On hold submissions will not expire and you should not delete/resubmit while on hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement scheduling and visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: How and where submissions appear once announced and how they are shown in user pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted items are set to be posted based on the automated announcement schedule. All submissions and updates associated with your arXiv account are shown on your user page; upon announcement articles move from the 'Article Submissions' to the 'Articles You Own' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not duplicate submissions (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid creating duplicate submissions while a submission is being processed or on hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making a duplicate submission, deleting and resubmitting, or otherwise duplicating while on hold will lead to further delays. If your submission is on hold, no immediate action is required unless editors contact you.
